Let \(AB=c\), \(A=(x,y)\), so \(c^2=x^2+y^2\). Since \(AC=9\),
\[
(6-x)^2+y^2=81 \implies 36-12x+c^2=81 \implies x=\frac{c^2-45}{12}.
\]

Let \(BM=BN=d\). Then
\[
N=(d,0),\qquad M=\left(\frac{dx}{c},\frac{dy}{c}\right).
\]
The line through \(M\) perpendicular to \(BC\) is \(X=\frac{dx}{c}\).  
The line through \(N\) perpendicular to \(AB\) has equation
\[
x(X-d)+yY=0.
\]
Their intersection is
\[
O=\left(\frac{dx}{c},\frac{dx(c-x)}{cy}\right).
\]
Thus the slope of \(BO\) is
\[
\frac{O_y}{O_x}=\frac{c-x}{y}.
\]

Since \(B,O,P\) are collinear and
\[
P=\left(\frac{4x+30}{9},\frac{4y}{9}\right),
\]
we get
\[
\frac{4y/9}{(4x+30)/9}=\frac{c-x}{y}
\]
so
\[
4y^2=(4x+30)(c-x).
\]
Using \(y^2=c^2-x^2\),
\[
4(c-x)(c+x)=(4x+30)(c-x).
\]
Since \(c\ne x\),
\[
4(c+x)=4x+30 \implies c=\frac{15}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
x=\frac{c^2-45}{12}=\frac{15}{16},\qquad 
y^2=c^2-x^2=\frac{14175}{256}.
\]
So
\[
P=\left(\frac{15}{4},\frac{5\sqrt{63}}{12}\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
BP^2=\left(\frac{15}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{5\sqrt{63}}{12}\right)^2
=\frac{225}{16}+\frac{1575}{144}=25.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{BP=5}.
\]
